assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic peak is a clean, calibrated standard ruler imprinted by sound waves in the early plasma and found in the late-time galaxy distribution. It gives a geometric, nature-based measurement of expansion history and dark energy that is largely independent of supernovae. For a theorist who thinks the string-theory treatment of dark energy needs clues from observation, this is exactly the kind of discovery that constrains the field. It is original, clear and has lasting use in precision cosmology.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections came from the SDSS luminous red galaxy sample (Eisenstein and collaborators) and the 2dFGRS power spectrum (Cole, Percival and collaborators). That gives a natural trio of one SDSS lead and two 2dF leads. The theoretical prediction of the feature has earlier roots (Peebles and Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich) that are not in the credited names, so the allocation relative to the theory origin is a real question for the committee.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed repeatedly and independently by SDSS-III/BOSS, WiggleZ, 6dFGS, eBOSS and now DESI. The interpretation is stable, with a recognised sound-horizon calibration, and nearly two decades have passed since discovery. Timely and mature, although the current Hubble tension and DESI hints of evolving dark energy are still being worked out.
uncertainties: Credit for the theoretical prediction of the acoustic feature may sit outside the supplied names.
Whether the prize would best be framed as the detection, or as the broader program of using BAO as a probe.
Current tensions in dark energy interpretation could change how the result is described, though not the discovery itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos by IceCube, and the 2018 association of a neutrino event with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and later the Galactic plane, opened a new window on the universe. It is a discovery made with a new instrument, built in Antarctic ice, in response to a long-standing question about the origin of cosmic rays. This is an existential-scale result about our place in the universe and an observation, not just an idea.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube over decades and is the single credited name. A prize for the instrument would normally involve more than one person, since the project depended on a large collaboration and on predecessors in neutrino telescopy (for example DUMAND, AMANDA, Baikal). With one credited name the supplied credit supports only a single laureate, and the committee would have to be careful that this does not understate other decisive leaders.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established and independently supported. Source identification is still limited to a few objects (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane), so the astrophysical picture is still developing. Recognition is reasonable now, though a few more years of source statistics would strengthen it.
uncertainties: Only one credited name, which may not reflect fair distribution of credit across IceCube and predecessor experiments.
Source population and production mechanism remain partly open.
I have not verified details of the 2018-2023 source associations independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains the flatness, the horizon problem and, with the Mukhanov-style quantum-fluctuation calculation, the origin of the nearly scale-invariant primordial spectrum seen in the CMB. It is among the most consequential ideas in modern cosmology. I value that the density-perturbation prediction has been tested by observation, and the details of the spectrum are well matched by data.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the original scenario, Linde the new and chaotic versions that actually work, and Mukhanov the quantum origin of perturbations. Starobinsky, whose earlier model is a key part of the history, is not among the supplied names, so the supplied credit is incomplete for a fair configuration. Choosing three from this list is defensible but imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Observations are consistent with inflation, but there is no direct detection of primordial gravitational waves or any unique signature of the inflaton. As someone who is wary of elegant theory without confirmation and who has worked on trans-Planckian effects in inflation, I regard the paradigm as strongly supported but not decisively established. This makes it somewhat premature as a prize, even though its impact is huge.
uncertainties: No primordial B-mode detection, and alternatives are not completely excluded.
Credit gap because Starobinsky is not in the credited names.
The paradigm has many model variants, which makes it difficult to name one specific discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The AdS/CFT correspondence reshaped quantum field theory and quantum gravity, connecting gravity to gauge theory and providing the main working framework for black-hole information, holography and strongly coupled systems. I know it well from my own work, and its originality and lasting influence on theory are beyond doubt.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture is the decisive origin; Polyakov and Witten (with Gubser and Klebanov, who are not in the supplied names) gave the dictionary that made it precise. The credited trio is reasonable, though Gubser and Klebanov are missing, and Maldacena alone could be argued to be the central figure.
assessment.maturity: It is a mathematically rich framework with many consistency checks, but the duality for realistic spacetimes, including the de Sitter case relevant to our universe, has no direct experimental confirmation of the kind the prize usually requires. Applications to quark-gluon plasma and condensed matter are suggestive and not decisive. Given my own scepticism, I rank it below the observationally grounded cosmology candidates.
uncertainties: No direct empirical test of the duality in nature.
Credit gap for Gubser and Klebanov.
Whether Maldacena alone is the true discovery owner.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays have reported evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries. This opens a new gravitational-wave band and is of direct interest to cosmology and gravity. The conceptual idea of the pulsar timing array and the long timing campaigns make this an experimental achievement of real depth.
assessment.attribution: The credited names represent the NANOGrav, EPTA and PPTA collaborations, but the decisive contributions are spread among many people and three or four collaborations (plus CPTA and earlier proposers such as Detweiler and Hellings and Downs). A fair three-person configuration is hard, which is a significant weakness.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 announcement has about 3 to 4 sigma significance for the Hellings-Downs correlation, not a discovery at the 5 sigma level, and the source (binaries versus new physics) is unresolved. This is probably premature; I would want further data releases and independent combination (IPTA) before taking it forward.
uncertainties: Significance below conventional discovery threshold.
Origin of the signal not settled.
Difficult attribution among several collaborations and earlier proposers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced the first full-sky, high-precision CMB maps, fixing the parameters of the standard cosmological model to a few percent and showing that the universe is flat with about 70 percent dark energy. The result is fundamental to our knowledge of dark energy and the composition of the universe.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Spergel led the analysis and cosmological interpretation, and Page was a core instrument and design scientist. This is a sensible trio. However, the CMB has been recognised twice (2006 COBE, 2019 cosmology), and Planck largely superseded WMAP's accuracy, so the committee may judge the WMAP-specific contribution to be an incremental refinement.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by Planck and other experiments, so maturity is high. The risk is not maturity but novelty: it is a precision measurement of an already-established picture and may be seen as already covered by earlier prizes.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with previous CMB and cosmology prizes.
Planck has superseded WMAP, so whether the WMAP-specific step counts as a distinct discovery is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and its observation in HgTe quantum wells launched topological insulators, one of the most influential developments in condensed matter. It is a clear, original, theory-then-experiment story: a definite prediction tested in nature, with deep conceptual impact on topology in band structures.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key theoretical proposal in graphene, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp's group realised in 2007. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not credited here, so the experimental half rests on Molenkamp while a major theory contribution is absent. The trio is defensible but not complete.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in multiple materials and by independent groups, with three-dimensional topological insulators and applications in many systems. The field is mature, and recognition could be considered timely or even overdue.
uncertainties: Credit gap for Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and for 3D topological insulator pioneers.
Competing candidate in the same field (B010) uses a different split of credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned strongly correlated quantum many-body physics into controllable laboratory experiments, with the observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and later quantum gas microscopy. It is conceptually clear and widely influential, although it is a platform more than a single decisive discovery.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) provided the theoretical proposal, Greiner and Bloch the experimental realisation of the Mott transition and microscopy. The list has four names, and I select the three that best span the theory proposal and experimental realisation; Cirac is a strong alternative, so the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Experiments are reproduced widely, and the platform is now mature. Its prize-worthiness is partly tied to future simulation results that go beyond what classical computers can do, so some of its significance is still developing.
uncertainties: Platform versus single discovery framing.
Allocation between Zoller and Cirac and the role of Jaksch, who is not credited.
Whether quantum simulation has yet produced unambiguous new physics.
